messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: kv-cache read error rate spike on prefix '/alpha/' and downstream latency SLO breaches. Affected: tenant-alpha. p95 latency 750ms, error_rate 18%. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example/incident/2423101234

maya (oncall): I'm on it, paged. starting triage. tagging @raj @jess @sam

jess (eng-sre): grabbing recent tails. seeing a lot of KV timeouts + cache misses on /v1/gen calls with long prompt prefixes. looks like heavy cold-prefetch traffic + correctness bypass churn. logs: `kv_read_timeout=timeout(150ms) count=432 in last 5m`

raj (runtime): is this correctness-driven bypass or pure load? any single tenant hotkeys?

sam (product): customers reporting 502s (tenant-alpha). support ticket 98712 shows repeated long-prefix requests from a single integration. may be a multipart prompt that bypasses prefix cache due to metadata mismatch.

maya (oncall): summary of actions i'm going to run now: 1) temporary tenant rate cap for tenant-alpha 2) disable prefix prefetch globally 3) enable per-prefix KV-bypass for keys where correctness flag present (avoid broad bypass) 4) route 25% of tenant-alpha traffic to fallback model variant (lower mem but stable)

maya (oncall): running commands:```sh
# limit tenant-alpha to 60 rps
rwctl tenants set-quota --tenant tenant-alpha --rps 60
# disable prefix prefetch globally
rwctl config set --key prefix_prefetch.enabled --value false
# mark specific prefix for bypass (correctness-only)
runtimectl cache prefix-set --prefix /alpha/long --bypass correct_only --duration 2h
# create traffic split
runtimectl traffic route --tenant tenant-alpha --split "primary:75,fallback-compact:25"
```

ops-bot: Deploy triggered: config changes applied by maya. change-id: cfg-242310-1. Rolling update to routing layer starting.

jess (eng-sre): I've also trimmed the redis read pool and bumped connection timeouts to reduce queuing. Applied a temporary KV read circuit: `kv.circuit.enabled=true` on nodes serving /alpha/*.

raj (runtime): good. also adding a soft rate-shaper at the inference gateway to smooth bursts:```yaml
inference_gateway:
  shaper:
    tenant-alpha:
      window_ms: 1000
      max_tokens: 5000
      burst: 1.2
```

maya (oncall): after the mitigations: p95 latency down to ~220ms, error_rate ~3% (observed across 3 consecutive 1-min windows). prom graph: https://dash.redwood.example/graph?i=2423101234

sam (product): support: drafting customer note, will send to tenant-alpha now: "We're seeing elevated errors earlier; we've applied temporary throttles and routing to fallback models. No data loss. We'll update within 2 hours." Lina, can you file a followup in CS?

lina (support): filing CS update and tagging accounts affected. ticket 98712 updated, customers notified.

jess (eng-sre): note: we enabled prefix bypass only for matching correctness flags. we DID NOT enable global KV bypass. this preserves cache benefits for other tenants. Keep an eye on cache_miss_rate metric.

raj (runtime): leaving a sticky note: rollback steps in order: 1) remove per-prefix bypass `runtimectl cache prefix-unset --prefix /alpha/long`, 2) re-enable `prefix_prefetch.enabled=true`, 3) remove tenant quota, 4) revert traffic split. Only revert if p95 stable <300ms for 10m.

maya (oncall): agreed. I'll monitor for 30m, then decide. @jordan you're next oncall at 23:00 PT — i'm going to hand this over early if it's still not fully stable.

ops-bot: autoscaling checkpoint: no further scaling events required, pool usage at 68%.

sam (product): quick note: we should consider a short-term model-variant for long-prefix requests to avoid KV-heavy prefetch. add to backlog: model routing policy for long-prefix heuristics.

jordan (next-oncall): ack, will join for handoff. ping me with the latest metrics before you step off.

maya (oncall): handoff summary -> jordan: incident id 2423101234, root cause: tenant-alpha long-prefix requests causing high cache miss and heavy prefetch leading to KV timeouts. Current mitigations: tenant-alpha quota=60rps, prefix_prefetch disabled globally, per-prefix bypass on /alpha/long for correctness, traffic split primary:75 / fallback-compact:25, redis pool trimmed, KV circuit enabled. Metrics now: p95 210-260ms, error_rate 2-4%. Customer comms sent. Runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood.example/kv-prefix-hotkey

jordan (next-oncall): taking over. Action items for me: keep mitigations for up to 2h, monitor p95 & error_rate, coordinate with runtime to schedule a controlled re-enable after stability window. If we see error_rate climb above 6% re-escalate to infra oncall.

maya (oncall): leaving a final note: do not re-enable global prefix_prefetch until we validate correctness flags are stable — worst-case flip: we keep prefetch disabled and focus on smarter prefetch policies. handing over now. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigations applied, severity reduced to P2. Pager clear for oncall -> active handoff to jordan. Logs archived to https://logs.redwood.example/2423101234

jordan (next-oncall): confirmed receipt. starting 2h watch window. will post updates every 30m or on any regression.

maya (oncall): thanks team. I'll sync tomorrow if needed for postmortem.

jess (eng-sre): leaving follow-ups: add CI test for prefix metadata mismatch, add alert for prefetch churn.

sam (product): adding customer remediation checklist to incident doc.

lina (support): monitoring customer replies. will escalate if any new outages.
